impact:
The consumer half of the Python-free story; depends on T-005a's artifacts existing and being verified. Design preserved in .story/sessions/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000/plan.md section 5.2.

Points already settled in review, each of which corrects an earlier draft:

- The replayer must REJECT an unknown mode or unindexed argv rather than falling back to "normal" — a silent fallback turns a missing artifact into a plausible wrong answer.
- Tree materialization needs content-bearing blobs; a hash-only manifest cannot reconstruct anything.
- Conformance must be a function called SYNCHRONOUSLY from inside golden.test.mjs, not a sibling test file. Node's runner may execute files independently or concurrently, so one file cannot gate another — an earlier revision claimed gating that does not hold.
- Mutations must target the MATERIALIZED TREE, not the manifest both sides read: alter a file byte, replace a symlink without following it, change the stale mtime, add an unexpected path, remove a required one.
- test:pure must cover ALL Python-free tests with a guard that every test file is classified exactly once, and must FAIL rather than skip on an unsupported platform.

Note for whoever picks this up: measured during T-005, npm test is not Python-free today — eight files in its glob (core, fixture-schema, pyrepr, resolve, table, tiebreak, unicode-parity, unicode-tables) spawn python3.

Also decide here, rather than carrying it as an unasserted requirement: permission bits are listed as a fixture prerequisite but are absent from the manifest schema and the Python builder inherits the umask. Either drop them as not contract-relevant, or set them deliberately in both builders.
title: T-005b: TS replayer, tree materialization, conformance, and a Python-free test:pure
